issues.explanation: In this poem, 滚滚 describes the Yangtze surging or rolling; it is not a panda nickname.
是非 is an ordinary lexical compound meaning right and wrong, not a fixed idiom here.
Here 在 is the verb “to remain/be present,” not a locative particle.
都 is an adverb meaning “all,” not a grammatical particle.
由 introduces the cause/source and functions as a preposition here, not a particle.
This span improperly combines the classifier/noun 人 with the personal name 张角, hiding the name.
issues.suggested_fix: Split as 人 + 张角, with 张角 kept as one name

issues.explanation: 南华老仙 is the name/title of one figure; splitting off 南华 obscures the proper name.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep 南华老仙 together as a name

issues.explanation: 十常侍 refers to the Ten Permanent Attendants, a group of eunuchs, not a generic byword for corruption.
天书 means heavenly/divine books or scriptures in this context, not an imperial edict.
符水 is the lexical term for talisman water used in ritual healing; splitting it hides the useful word.
和 links two objects, 治病 and 咒术, as a conjunction; it is not a particle.
The pinyin for 岁 is incorrect; 岁在甲子 means “in the year of Jiazi.”
In 天公将军, 将军 is the military title “general,” not a place-name element.
In 地公将军, 将军 is the military title “general,” not a place-name element.
In 人公将军, 将军 is the military title “general,” not a place-name element.
投军 is a lexical verb meaning to enlist or join the army; splitting it hides a useful word.
关羽 is a personal name and must not be split into separate lexical segments.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep 关羽 together as one name

issues.explanation: 同心 means “with one heart/in unity” compositionally here and is not functioning as a lexicalized idiom.
麾下 means under someone’s command or banner, not “troops” itself.

孝廉 is a historical recommendation title and should be kept together rather than split into 孝 and 廉.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep 孝廉 together; “filial and incorrupt (recommendation title)”
